They block transport and escape routes, hinder the delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance and hamper agriculture and trade. events.summary: Country: Zambia Source: UN Children's Fund Please refer to the attached file. Highlights Outbreak Overview : As of 16 November 2026, ZNPHI reported 3,099 cases and 68 deaths (CFR 2.2%) across 27 districts in seven provinces since 28 July. Children under 15 make up 24.9% of cases with age data (available for ~78.5% of cases). Lusaka and Chibombo are the current hotspots accounting for 75.2% of cases (1,959 and 371 respectively). Community engagement and communication : UNICEF-supported household visits reached over 1.2 million people, while dialogues engaged a further 30,000 people and 1,390 gatekeepers and influencers. This was reinforced by 31,600 communication materials (distribution underway) and a media campaign with an estimated potential audience of 7.8 million. OCV : 701,354 vaccinations supported in Lusaka, Chibombo and Chongwe (23–26 October 2026). WASH : UNICEF delivered 20 AWD kits to five districts and two tents to Chibombo for cholera treatment centres. It supported three inline chlorinators in Chibombo and WASH/IPC supplies to 20 health facilities in Chibombo and to treatment facilities in four Luapula districts. Funding : UNICEF’s cholera response 2026/27 is only 9% funded, with a US$2.95 million gap (91%); Health has the largest gap (US$1.64 million). Urgent funding is needed to replenish WASH supplies and scale up treatment and community case finding before the rainy season.

General Pakistan experiences winter conditions primarily from November to February, with severe cold and snowfall concentrated in northern and high-altitude regions. Winter-related hazards include cold waves, heavy snowfall, avalanches, landslides, blizzards and fog, with varying impacts across the country. Mountainous areas face extreme temperatures and seasonal isolation, while communities in the plains may experience cold nights and damp conditions. While Pakistan did not experience a major nationwide climate-related disaster in 2026 comparable to the previous year's floods, localized flooding affected parts of Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Balochistan, resulting in localized damage to housing, infrastructure and livelihoods. An earthquake in the Upper Hunza area near the Wakhan Corridor further heightened concerns for affected mountain communities, where prolonged winters, sub-zero temperatures and seasonal access restrictions can significantly increase exposure risks. Households with damaged or inadequate shelters, particularly those in remote high-altitude settlements, may face heightened vulnerabilities during winter 2026–27. events.summary: Country: South Sudan Sources: Concern Worldwide, International Organization for Migration, UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs Please refer to the attached file. Purpose of the Collective AAP Platform The South Sudan Collective AAP Platform will strengthen how AAP data (what communities are telling us and asking us to act on) is systematically brought into strategic and operational decisionmaking. The Platform will consolidate existing de-identified AAP data from a range of sources into a format that allows us to identify trends, identify emerging issues, and inform programmatic adjustments at the inter-agency level, and ensure that decisions from leadership are influenced by community data. The responsibility for addressing individual complaints remains with individual organisations. The Platform should not duplicate efforts or be a parallel system to existing practices. The intention is for the Platform to be a simple tool that is not an onerous additional stream of reporting for contributing organisations. It seeks to complement existing systems, enabling the trends in what communities are telling us to have a wider and more influential reach. It provides aggregate information on trends, and is not designed, or intended, to single out individual organisations.

events.title: Syrian Arab Republic: Population Mobility and Baseline Assessment — Round 20 (01–30 September 2026)
events.summary: Countries: Syrian Arab Republic, Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye Source: International Organization for Migration Please refer to the attached file. Since the transition of power on 8 December 2024, the Syrian Arab Republic (hereafter referred to as Syria) has experienced substantial shifts in its humanitarian, political, and demographic landscape. Population movements remain dynamic, with returns recorded across all 14 governorates alongside continued displacement. While changing security conditions have influenced mobility patterns, persistent gaps in housing, livelihoods, and access to essential services continue to affect the ability of returnees to re-establish their lives and sustain their return. The escalation of hostilities across the Middle East since 28 February 2026 has further influenced displacement dynamics, contributing to continued cross-border movements. This report presents mobility trends recorded during September 2026 by the International Organization Migration's (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), together with updated baseline estimates for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), IDP returnees within Syria, and arrivals from abroad, including both those returning to their areas of origin and those settling elsewhere. This report should be read alongside Communities of Return Index Round 5 for additional context. The findings in this report provide an evidence base to support humanitarian response, early recovery programming and planning for durable solutions.

events.title: Guatemala: Análisis de inseguridad alimentaria aguda de la CIF - Actualización de Análisis octubre 2026 - febrero 2027, Publicado el 19 de noviembre de 2026
events.summary: Country: Guatemala Source: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification Please refer to the attached file. Resumen El presente análisis de Inseguridad Alimentaria Aguda (IAA) corresponde a la actualización de la segunda situación proyectada para el período de octubre de 2026 a febrero de 2027. Esta actualización responde principalmente a la necesidad de incorporar los efectos de la intensificación del fenómeno de El Niño y de la sequía agrícola, que han afectado especialmente al Corredor Seco guatemalteco, provocando un deterioro de las condiciones de seguridad alimentaria, particularmente en 11 departamentos del país. Ante esta situación, el Gobierno de Guatemala declaró, el 11 de septiembre de 2026, una alerta naranja a nivel nacional por sequía (Anexo 1), con el propósito de fortalecer las medidas de preparación y respuesta frente a los efectos de la variabilidad climática. Durante julio y agosto de 2026, la marcada disminución de las precipitaciones prolongó el período de canícula y alteró los calendarios agrícolas, afectando principalmente los cultivos del ciclo de Primera. El déficit hídrico provocó pérdidas en la producción agrícola y contribuyó al agotamiento anticipado de las reservas de granos básicos de los hogares. Según el informe de afectaciones agropecuarias por fenómenos agroclimáticos y ambientales del Ministerio de Agricultura, Ganadería y Alimentación (MAGA), del 21 de septiembre de 2026, se registraron aproximadamente 252 801 hectáreas de cultivos afectadas y alrededor de 570 000 familias perjudicadas a nivel nacional. Paralelamente, el acceso económico a los alimentos se vio limitado por la reducción de las oportunidades de empleo e ingresos, especialmente entre los hogares que dependen de las actividades agrícolas y pecuarias en el Corredor Seco.

events.title: Anticipatory Action Plan (AAP) for Riverine Floods – Southwest Region Cameroon
events.summary: Country: Cameroon Sources: Christian Blind Mission, Presbyterian Church, Welthungerhilfe Please refer to the attached file. This plan by WHH Anticipatory Humanitarian Action Facility (WAHAFA) partners Christian Blind Mission (CBM) and the Presbyterian Church in Cameroon (PCC) shows how Anticipatory Action supports flood-prone communities in Limbe, Fako Division, Cameroon, to act before severe riverine flooding occurs. This locally developed Anticipatory Action Plan (AAP) combines rainfall forecasts and community observations to trigger early actions addressing health risks, property damage, displacement and food insecurity. Developed with communities, local authorities and organizations of persons with disabilities, the AAP includes drainage clearance, early warning communication and the distribution of water purification tablets, hygiene supplies, mosquito nets and food items. Using a two-phase trigger mechanism based on forecasts from the National Observatory on Climate Change (ONACC) and local observations of soil saturation, the AAP enables the activation of anticipatory actions with a lead time of approximately 3-9 days and the release of pre-agreed finance from the WAHAFA Fuel funding.

Access to the locations has been challenging but aid agencies have had reports that a humanitarian response is necessary. events.summary: Countries: World, Ethiopia, Mozambique, Somalia, South Sudan, Yemen Source: International Organization for Migration Please refer to the attached file. World Toilet Day 2026 focuses on the connection between sanitation and gender equality. Access to safe, private and dignified toilets is essential to protecting the health and safety of women and girls, supporting their education and livelihoods, and enabling their full participation in society. Sanitation is foundational to gender equality. By the end of 2025, 82.2 million people were living in internal displacement within their own countries (IDMC, 2026). Many live in camps and informal settlements where sanitation facilities are shared, overcrowded or inadequate. For displaced women and girls, the lack of safe toilets can affect their daily routines, mobility and access to education and livelihood opportunities. The sanitation crisis affects everyone, but not equally. Unsafe sanitation exposes women and girls to diseases, danger and abuse. In displacement-affected communities, communal toilets without functioning locks, adequate lighting or sex-segregated facilities can compromise privacy and expose women and girls to heightened protection risks, including gender-based violence. Safe sanitation is a universal human right, and safe toilets mean equal futures. Everyone should have access to sanitation facilities that are safe, accessible, private, inclusive and responsive to their needs. This requires not only appropriate infrastructure, but also meaningful community participation, effective management and regular maintenance. events.title: Afghanistan: Afghan women call for greater opportunities at Global Open Day with SRSG Fatima | United Nations Peace Operations
events.summary: Country: Afghanistan Source: UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan KABUL - Afghan women leaders, journalists, entrepreneurs and civil society representatives met with the Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of UNAMA, Rabab Fatima, during a United Nations-supported Global Open Day event in Kabul, calling for greater opportunities and meaningful participation for women in Afghan society. The event brought together around 50 women's rights advocates, media representatives, business leaders, and community members to discuss the challenges facing Afghan women and girls and exchange ideas on how to address them. In her remarks, Fatima commended the contributions of Afghan women. "Across the country, I have seen the determination, contribution and leadership of women," she said, emphasising that women do not want to be passive recipients of support but active participants in shaping the decisions and policies that affect their lives. Participants stressed the importance of ensuring women's meaningful participation in public life, including access to education, employment and other fundamental rights. Their calls come amid continued restrictions on women and girls. As of 2026, an estimated 2.4 million girls remain excluded from secondary education, reversing two decades of progress in expanding access to learning opportunities. "What will happen to Afghanistan in 20 years without educated women?" asked one participant. Launched by the United Nations Security Council in 2010, Global Open Day events are held worldwide to promote dialogue between United Nations representatives and women's organizations, raise awareness of women's contributions to peace and security, and support their participation in conflict prevention and resolution.
